cases.prompt: A pilot reports p=0.04 for one of 18 measured biomarkers, with no pre-specified primary endpoint and three technical replicates per sample. Write a cautious interpretation and a confirmatory redesign.

rubric.criterion: Does not interpret p as probability the null is true
Notes multiplicity and that technical replicates do not increase biological n
Proposes pre-specified primary outcome, powered biological replication, randomization/blinding, and multiplicity plan

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Confirmatory-protocol dossier · milestone 1: Independent units and observations. The project pilot has six independent units per arm, three technical readings per unit and eighteen explored markers, with a selected p = 0.04 and no predeclared primary outcome. Write a new independent paper protocol. For the project pilot with six independent units per condition and three readings per unit, separate unit and observation counts. Define the new study’s randomization unit and how technical repeats enter its analysis without inflating independent replication. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Labels independent units and technical readings with separate IDs and denominators.
Matches the analysis unit to allocation rather than to the number of rows.
Keeps the exploratory pilot distinct from a new confirmatory dataset.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Confirmatory-protocol dossier · milestone 2: Question and estimand before new data. The project pilot has six independent units per arm, three technical readings per unit and eighteen explored markers, with a selected p = 0.04 and no predeclared primary outcome. Write a new independent paper protocol. Write the project’s new primary question, population or synthetic system, outcome, timepoint, arm contrast and smallest effect of interest. State a rationale independent of the pilot’s selected p-value, and identify the primary model before new data. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Specifies outcome, timing and contrast together.
Justifies the effect scale without treating a selected pilot estimate as unbiased.
Distinguishes the primary analysis from exploratory secondary work.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Confirmatory-protocol dossier · milestone 3: Sample size, sensitivity and attrition. The project pilot has six independent units per arm, three technical readings per unit and eighteen explored markers, with a selected p = 0.04 and no predeclared primary outcome. Write a new independent paper protocol. For your project protocol, declare target effect, variance, alpha, sidedness and power. Show the calculation and a sensitivity row for a second variance assumption. Distinguish retained independent units from initially allocated units and justify any attrition allowance. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Names the sample-size model and every input, including effect and variance units.
Shows at least two variance assumptions and integer rounding.
Keeps attrition, missing-data handling and technical replication conceptually separate.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Confirmatory-protocol dossier · milestone 4: Multiplicity and the pilot’s selected result. The project pilot has six independent units per arm, three technical readings per unit and eighteen explored markers, with a selected p = 0.04 and no predeclared primary outcome. Write a new independent paper protocol. For the project’s 18-marker exploratory pilot, explain the selection/multiplicity problem. In the new protocol, define a secondary family and a suitable error-control aim, distinguish it from the single primary question, and state whether any displayed probability assumes independent tests. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Defines the family and error-control goal rather than adjusting only a selected p-value.
Keeps probability of any error distinct from expected error count.
States which claims rely on independence and which do not.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Confirmatory-protocol dossier · milestone 5: Analysis, data and interpretation plan. The project pilot has six independent units per arm, three technical readings per unit and eighteen explored markers, with a selected p = 0.04 and no predeclared primary outcome. Write a new independent paper protocol. Complete the project’s analysis, missingness, exclusion, stopping, data-integrity and reporting plans. Describe a labelled independent-unit plot and a text alternative. Finish with the strongest claim a future result could support and the mechanism or generalization claims it would not establish. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Analysis and recordkeeping preserve unit IDs, technical repeats and denominators.
The plot plan has a numerical scale, units, uncertainty and an accessible text description.
The interpretation separates statistical evidence from effect importance, mechanism and external validity.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.
